items.title: Industry Leaders Unite in Open Secure AI Alliance for AI Safety and Security
items.summary: Industry leaders have formed the Open Secure AI Alliance to develop and share open technologies to safeguard software and agents in the age of AI. The alliance aims to remediate and disclose vulnerabilities using open technologies and provide defenders with open, frontier tools they can trust and control. Partners include major companies such as NVIDIA, Adobe, and Cisco, which will contribute to the development of new cybersecurity tools and techniques.
items.audio_script:
From NVIDIA Blog, "Industry Leaders Unite in Open Secure AI Alliance for AI Safety and Security," a group of major companies has formed the Open Secure AI Alliance to develop and share open technologies to safeguard software and agents in the age of AI. This alliance aims to remediate and disclose vulnerabilities using open technologies and provide defenders with open, frontier tools they can trust and control. Industry leaders have partnered to contribute to the development of new cybersecurity tools and techniques, solidifying their commitment to ensuring AI safety and security.

The partnership was formed through a collaborative effort, bringing together industry giants such as NVIDIA, Adobe, and Cisco to address the growing concerns surrounding AI's impact on software and agents. By pooling their expertise and resources, these companies will create open-source technologies that can be used by developers worldwide. This approach ensures transparency, trustworthiness, and control over the cybersecurity tools and techniques developed for this alliance.

The Open Secure AI Alliance marks a significant step forward in the industry's pursuit of AI safety and security. items.title: Misleading AI-generated doctors pose ‘huge danger to public safety’
items.summary: AI-generated doctors are spreading dubious health advice on TikTok, posing a huge danger to public safety. Research found that 84% of top health-related videos were classed as AI-generated or AI-assisted content, with some videos receiving up to 2.5m views. Disproven myths about cancer and other health issues have been spread through these fake doctor accounts, which are often designed to resemble real doctors. Platforms like TikTok must do more to stop the rise of dangerous fake medical advice.
items.audio_script: From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Misleading AI-generated doctors pose ‘huge danger to public safety’". Research has found that a significant proportion of health-related content on TikTok is being generated by artificial intelligence, with 84% of top health-related videos classed as AI-generated or AI-assisted content. These AI-generated doctors are spreading dubious health advice, receiving up to 2.5 million views and potentially putting public safety at risk. The study's methodology involved analyzing over 1,000 videos, including those from high-profile accounts, to determine the extent of AI-generated content on the platform. The results show that these fake medical accounts often mimic real doctors' styles and are designed to promote disproven myths about cancer and other health issues.

items.title: How AI is expanding what people do at work
items.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is expanding what workers can do at work, as demonstrated by new OpenAI research. Workers using ChatGPT are taking on tasks typically associated with multiple roles. This shift in job responsibilities is reshaping traditional job boundaries.
items.audio_script: From OpenAI - News, "How AI is expanding what people do at work." New research from OpenAI has shown that workers are taking on tasks typically associated with multiple roles when using ChatGPT, a conversational AI tool. The study demonstrates how AI capabilities are expanding job responsibilities, effectively reshaping traditional job boundaries as workers utilize the technology to handle an increased workload. Researchers employed ChatGPT in various workplace settings, allowing employees to leverage its features and capabilities for tasks that usually fall within multiple roles. The results reveal significant changes in how people work with AI tools like ChatGPT. This expansion of job responsibilities highlights the evolving role of human workers as they adapt to new technologies and collaborate more effectively with AI systems.

items.title: NVIDIA Harnesses Vera CPU to Speed Up Design of Next-Generation CPUs and GPUs

Early testing on selected production-class workflows demonstrates up to 1.5x higher performance with applications like Cadence Jasper and Synopsys VCS. NVIDIA is deploying Vera across its own engineering workflows to accelerate each workload with the compute architecture best suited to the task.

items.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra Leads Open Models on Accuracy and Efficiency in Agentic RTL Coding
items.summary: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra leads open models on accuracy and efficiency in agentic RTL coding, achieving a 97.1% average pass rate across nine agentic RTL task categories. It uses up to 71% fewer tokens per iteration compared to Kimi K2.6 while maintaining the highest average pass rate. Nematron 3 Ultra's hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture improves throughput efficiency by reducing attention cost and KV-cache footprint, delivering up to 5X higher throughput and 30% lower costs compared to other open models.

This achievement was made possible by the use of up to 71% fewer tokens per iteration compared to Kimi K2.6, while maintaining the highest average pass rate. Nematron 3 Ultra's hybrid Mamba-Attention architecture improved throughput efficiency by reducing attention cost and KV-cache footprint, delivering up to 5X higher throughput and 30% lower costs compared to other open models.

items.title: NVIDIA Cosmos-H-Dreams: Bringing Real-Time Generative Simulation to Surgical Robotics
items.summary: NVIDIA Cosmos-H-Dreams is a real-time, action-conditioned generative simulator for surgical robotics that brings physical robotic platforms from teleoperation toward increasingly capable vision-language-action policies. It distills the capabilities of the Cosmos-H-Surgical-Simulator into a causal, few-step student model and serves it through FlashDreams, an accelerated streaming-inference library.
items.audio_script:
From Hugging Face Blog, "NVIDIA Cosmos-H-Dreams: Bringing Real-Time Generative Simulation to Surgical Robotics". NVIDIA has made a breakthrough in developing a real-time generative simulator for surgical robotics, dubbed Cosmos-H-Dreams. This simulator enables physical robotic platforms to learn from teleoperation and evolve into more capable vision-language-action policies through action-conditioned generative simulation.

The researchers at Hugging Face have distilled the capabilities of the Cosmos-H-Surgical-Simulator into a causal, few-step student model, which is served through FlashDreams, an accelerated streaming-inference library. This achievement demonstrates the potential for real-time generative simulation in surgical robotics, allowing for more precise and efficient procedures.

The implications of this technology are significant, as it has the potential to transform the field of surgical robotics and enable more sophisticated robotic systems that can adapt to complex medical scenarios in real-time.

items.title: Closing the data loop in AI-driven drug discovery
items.source: MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech
items.summary: AI is being used in drug discovery to identify potential new chemical compounds, design drug candidates, and optimize existing ones, with the goal of reducing development time and costs. Early applications of AI in this field show promise, but also highlight a need for robust and authentic data as well as integration into lab systems. The lack of complete and diverse data can lead to bias and inaccurate predictions, making it difficult to identify high-quality candidates for clinical trials. To address this, vendors are developing tools to verify the integrity of scientific images and datasets, enabling the creation of more reliable AI models.
items.audio_script: From MIT Technology Review - AI & Emerging Tech, "Closing the data loop in AI-driven drug discovery," researchers are making progress in using AI to accelerate the development of new pharmaceuticals by identifying potential chemical compounds, designing and optimizing existing ones. According to a recent study, early applications of AI in this field have shown significant promise, with AI algorithms able to analyze large datasets to predict the efficacy and safety of novel compounds. To address concerns about data quality and reliability, vendors are developing tools that can verify the integrity of scientific images and datasets, which is essential for creating more accurate and trustworthy AI models. This development is expected to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of drug discovery processes in the pharmaceutical industry.

items.title: Optical Tech Would Update a Robot’s AI on the Fly
items.summary: Researchers have developed an optical tech that can project light directly onto a chip, enabling data streaming with less energy. This innovation could potentially be used to update robot AI models on the fly without relying on energy-demanding electrical connections. The technology uses an optical receiver to transmit data wirelessly. It has the potential to improve robot AI efficiency and reduce energy consumption.
items.audio_script: From IEEE Spectrum - Artificial Intelligence, "Optical Tech Would Update a Robot’s AI on the Fly," researchers have developed an optical technology that enables data streaming with less energy by projecting light directly onto a chip. By harnessing this capability, researchers believe that robot AI efficiency can be improved while reducing energy consumption.

items.title: A Single RL Policy Produced Surprisingly Watchable Football
items.summary: A single football policy was trained for 1 million PPO timesteps in an empty environment, without playing against an opponent. During inference, multiple copies of the same policy were assigned to opposing teams, resulting in surprisingly entertaining matches. The agents competed for possession, took shots, and occasionally defended their own goal, demonstrating emergent defensive behaviors. No explicit training or coordination was used.
items.audio_script: From RL Reddit, "A Single RL Policy Produced Surprisingly Watchable Football," a single football policy was trained for 1 million PPO timesteps in an empty environment, resulting in surprisingly entertaining matches. The agents, competing against each other without explicit training or coordination, demonstrated emergent defensive behaviors such as taking shots, defending their own goal, and occasionally conceding possession to the opposing team's control. Multiple copies of the same policy were assigned to opposing teams, allowing for multiple matches to be simulated simultaneously in the empty environment, where the agents competed for possession, showcased teamwork-like behavior, and even adapted to each other's strategies over time.

items.title: How to Efficiently Prompt Claude Code
items.summary:
To optimize the way you prompt LLMs, start by being explicit about what you want, including how to test the implementation, and clarifying any ambiguities. A good prompt should ask the model to discover ambiguities and discuss them with you. Use transcription tools instead of typing your prompts out, as they save time and allow for more context to be included.

Telling the model how to test is also crucial, such as specifying what tests need to be run and how to ensure correct implementation. Having a discussion with the model before implementing a feature or resolving a bug is essential to align your understanding with the agent's assumptions.

HTML reports can help visualize the output of the coding agents, making it easier for you to provide feedback and understand complex decisions. Reports can include options, context, pros and cons, and visualizations such as diagrams and flow charts, allowing for a more efficient workflow and better collaboration between humans and LLMs.
items.audio_script: From Towards Data Science, "How to Efficiently Prompt Claude Code," experts have discovered that optimizing LLM prompts requires explicitness and clarity, with a focus on testing implementation and resolving ambiguities. To achieve this, users should employ transcription tools to save time and include more context in their prompts. Furthermore, providing clear instructions for testing is crucial, such as specifying necessary tests and ensuring correct implementation through discussion before feature development or bug resolution. HTML reports can aid in visualizing output, enabling humans to provide feedback and collaborate with LLMs more efficiently. This approach promises to streamline workflows and enhance collaboration between humans and AI agents.

items.title: How to Give an LLM Agent a Browser
items.summary: A browser-using agent can be built with OpenAI Agents SDK and Playwright MCP by creating an observation channel using structured page information, such as Document Object Model or accessibility tree, and an action channel using element-targeted browser actions. The agent connects to Azure OpenAI and sets up the Playwright MCP server, which exposes tools for the LLM agent to interact with the browser. A concrete task is given to the agent, which resolves a customer support request through a web-based support console by navigating to the application, investigating the case, determining and applying the appropriate resolution, and reporting the outcome.
items.audio_script: From Towards Data Science, "How to Give an LLM Agent a Browser," a team of researchers successfully integrated Large Language Models with browsers using the OpenAI Agents SDK and Playwright MCP. They achieved this by creating an observation channel utilizing structured page information such as Document Object Model or accessibility tree, and an action channel using element-targeted browser actions, allowing the agent to interact with the browser seamlessly. The agent was then connected to Azure OpenAI and set up the Playwright MCP server, exposing tools for the LLM agent to navigate through a web-based support console. Upon receiving a concrete task, the agent resolved a customer support request by investigating the case, determining the appropriate resolution, and reporting the outcome. This breakthrough demonstrates the potential for further development in hybrid AI systems combining human-like language understanding with browser-based automation capabilities.

items.title: Corporate America may be using AI to cut jobs, but small businesses are using it to keep them
items.summary: Reports of wide-scale replacement of workers by AI are overblown, as small businesses use it to help their employees work better. According to the Department of Labor, there has been a 9% increase in people employed since mid-2021, with most small businesses reporting continued job gains among their customers. Small businesses are using AI to automate tasks such as quote creation, customer support, and data review, freeing up staff to focus on more productive work and serving more customers.
items.audio_script:
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "Corporate America may be using AI to cut jobs, but small businesses are using it to keep them". According to recent reports, corporate America's widespread adoption of artificial intelligence has led to exaggerated claims that the technology is on the brink of replacing workers en masse. However, a more nuanced picture emerges when focusing on the use of AI by small businesses, where the technology is being employed to augment employee productivity rather than replace them. In fact, the Department of Labor has reported a 9% increase in employment since mid-2021, with most small businesses continuing to report job gains among their customers. By automating tasks such as quote creation, customer support, and data review, small businesses are freeing up staff to focus on more productive work and serving more customers. As a result, the trend suggests that AI is being used in ways that complement human labor rather than supplant it.

This trend marks an important shift in the narrative around AI's impact on employment, one that could lead to a greater understanding of the technology's potential benefits when harnessed effectively.

items.title: What If We Got AI Right? by Eleanor Drage review – avoiding apocalypse
items.summary: Eleanor Drage's book "What If We Got AI Right?" aims to provide an alternative vision of what AI could be, but it falls short by failing to offer meaningful answers. The author argues that big tech companies prioritize profit and power over ethics, leading to biased algorithms, exploitation, and environmental harm. While Drage presents some convincing critiques of the tech industry, her arguments sometimes become rushed or sloppy. Her proposed solutions, such as community-based AI projects, are underwhelming and lack clarity on how AI can specifically contribute to a better future.
items.audio_script:
From The Guardian - Artificial Intelligence, "What If We Got AI Right? by Eleanor Drage review – avoiding apocalypse". This story assesses the book's arguments and findings on how big tech companies' prioritization of profit over ethics affects the development of artificial intelligence. 

Eleanor Drage's book critiques the tech industry for prioritizing profit and power over ethics, leading to biased algorithms and exploitation. She argues that community-based AI projects could be an alternative solution, but her proposed solutions are underwhelming and lack clarity on how AI can specifically contribute to a better future. The author presents some convincing critiques of the tech industry, highlighting the need for more responsible AI development. While Drage's book provides valuable insights into the issues surrounding AI, its limitations become apparent in its failure to offer meaningful answers to these problems.

Drage's work falls short due to its inability to provide a clear roadmap for responsible AI development. Her proposed solutions are often vague or lacking in detail, leaving room for speculation about their feasibility and potential impact. Despite this, her book serves as a useful starting point for discussions about the ethics of AI development, highlighting the need for greater accountability and transparency within the industry.

As the AI landscape continues to evolve, it remains essential to scrutinize its development and implementation to prevent potential pitfalls and ensure a more equitable future for all.

items.title: Why you should become niche famous
items.summary: Becoming "niche famous" means building a reputation among 1,000 like-minded individuals rather than trying to go viral with a large, but less engaged audience. A recent in-person event, called "Niche Famous", brought together 520 people who wanted to build a personal brand online and struggled due to other commitments. The event was a success, with attendees coming from various professional fields and having real substance. The true value of the event wasn't the advice or tips, but rather the connections made and shared experiences among like-minded individuals.
items.audio_script:
From Hannah Zhang, "Why you should become niche famous". A recent in-person event, called "Niche Famous", brought together 520 people who wanted to build a personal brand online and struggled due to other commitments. The event, which was a success, featured attendees from various professional fields, including marketing, entertainment, and technology. The true value of the event lay not in the advice or tips provided by speakers, but rather the connections made among like-minded individuals and shared experiences that highlighted the importance of community and authenticity.

The organizers of "Niche Famous" aimed to create a space where attendees could learn from each other's struggles and successes without the distractions of a large online audience. By limiting the guest list to around 1,000 people, they fostered an environment conducive to meaningful conversations and collaborations. The event was notable for its focus on real substance over superficial advice, with speakers sharing their own experiences and insights rather than relying on pre-packaged tips.

The success of "Niche Famous" suggests that niche fame may be a more effective strategy for building a personal brand online than traditional methods, which often rely on going viral to achieve widespread recognition. As the event demonstrates, connections made among like-minded individuals can lead to lasting collaborations and opportunities.

items.title: An Inside Look at the Relay Market Powering Token Resellers and Fraud
items.summary: A market has grown up in China around reselling LLM tokens at a discount by pooling API keys, often using free trials, proxying through support bots, or stolen credit cards. Resellers sell access to an LLM proxy offering significant discounts on regular API pricing. The software used for these proxies is open source and can be used to balance requests across a pool of API credentials. LLM vendors need to improve their API key caps to prevent abuse.
items.audio_script: From Simon Willison's Weblog, "An Inside Look at the Relay Market Powering Token Resellers and Fraud," a growing market in China has emerged where resellers pool API keys to offer discounted access to Large Language Model (LLM) tokens. Using free trials, proxy servers, or stolen credit cards, these resellers can balance requests across a pool of compromised API credentials, allowing for significant price cuts on regular API pricing. The software behind these proxies is open-source and can be used to manage the allocation of API keys. LLM vendors are now under pressure to increase their API key caps to prevent exploitation.

items.title: Cloud-Native Evaluation-as-a-Service: A Microservices Architecture for Scalable AI Monitoring with Conformal Guarantees
items.summary: Lei Yang presents EaaS, a cloud-native reference architecture for scalable AI monitoring with conformal guarantees. The six stateless Kubernetes microservices include conformal prediction, calibration assessment, drift detection, fairness monitoring, a DAG-based pipeline orchestrator, and result storage. The system is validated through empirical coverage, marginal conformal guarantee, and accuracy of fairness monitoring on the UCI Adult Income dataset. EaaS achieves sub-2ms p99 latency at batch size 100 with conformal prediction and calibration services.

items.title: On the Depth Scalability of Logic Gate Networks
items.summary: Logic Gate Networks (LGNs) do not reliably benefit from increased depth due to optimization collapse in deep relaxed LGNs and a topology-induced limitation. The authors introduce Input-Anchored Logic Gate Networks (IALGNs), which preserve a computational spine while conditioning every layer on the original input, achieving consistent fixed-width depth and accuracy improvements beyond 100 layers.

items.title: MotifRole-Diff: Risk-Optimal Role-Aware Corruption for Masked Molecular Graph Diffusion
items.summary: Masked discrete diffusion for molecular graph generation applies uniform corruption schedules to all tokens, treating heterogeneous components as equally difficult and important. MotifRole-Diff introduces a role-aware corruption process that allocates masking rates according to empirically measured denoising difficulty and perturbation impact while preserving the model architecture and clean sequence space. This approach improves validity on QM9 from 0.905 to 0.944, reducing FCD from 1.701 to 1.609, and on MOSES from 0.920 to 0.938, reducing FCD from 2.125 to 1.850.

items.title: Toward User-Conditioned Evaluation of Personal LLM Agents under Temporal Interventions
items.summary: Existing agent benchmarks often evaluate capabilities in isolation, such as tool benchmarks testing invocation under fixed APIs or memory benchmarks testing recall or forgetting. A new protocol requires replaying the same temporal intervention across different persistent user-conditioned states to measure how failures propagate across agent components. The authors propose a minimal benchmark design and candidate reporting metrics for user-conditioned adaptation, highlighting a gap in existing literature. This claim is scoped as a focused gap analysis with bounded literature coverage.

items.title: Measuring the Dependency Gap: Diagnosing Inter-Column Fidelity in Tabular Generative Models
items.summary: Researchers Jie Zhang introduced a new metric to diagnose inter-column fidelity in tabular generative models. The current metrics, such as the logistic-regression C2ST and pairwise Trend score, are found to be insensitive to inter-column dependency. A new dependency-aware diagnostic method was proposed, which separates the classifier's performance into marginal, dependency, and numerical-categorical cross components. Applying this method to a state-of-the-art flow-matching generator (TabbyFlow/EF-VFM), it revealed a real dependency gap that standard metrics miss, pointing to the absence of direct dependency supervision rather than a capacity or structural limit.

items.title: Quasi-Monte Carlo Initialization for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC) weight initialization improves training convergence in meta-reinforcement learning for unseen continuous control environments, outperforming modern orthogonal defaults. QMC meta-priors bound a population-based search and aggregate an optimal prior from baseline tasks, leading to better performance compared to orthogonal orientation.

items.title: Multi-Horizon Consistency as Geometry: When Latent Dynamics Contract, and When They Do Not
items.summary: Raising the weight on multi-step latent agreement (lambda) from 0 to 0.8 halves the prediction error E20 and cuts the expansion proxy L20,q95 from 4.96 +/- 2.01 to 1.01 +/- 0.06 in a study of video predictors on Moving-MNIST, with four out of six seeds crossing the threshold L<1 at lambda=0.8.

items.title: Adjustment Speed as a Safety Constraint for Nonstationary Reinforcement Learning
items.summary: Adjustment speed as a safety constraint for nonstationary reinforcement learning proposes defining safety in terms of adaptation feasibility. The framework estimates adaptation demand and compares it with the agent's achievable adaptation capacity, proactively tightening the admissible action set and activating an action-level shield to reduce unsafe behavior before violations occur. Experiments show that this approach primarily reduces safety violations in short-horizon windows aligned with context changes, supporting adaptation feasibility as a practical safety principle for reinforcement learning under nonstationarity.

items.title: A Drift Stable Quantum Federated Learning for Intelligent Services
items.summary: A Drift Stable Quantum Federated Learning for Intelligent Services proposes a framework called DUQFL-Prox, which combines adaptive unfolded SPSA updates and a proximal term to keep local models close to global models. Each client performs these updates using step-specific optimization parameters learned by a lightweight controller. Experiments show that DUQFL-Prox improves stability, generalization, and client fairness in financial fraud and genomic classification tasks compared to standard QFL baselines.

items.title: Prior laundering: learned priors with inherited, undetectable overconfidence
items.summary: Learned generative priors are increasingly used in ill-posed Bayesian inverse problems, but training one requires truths that are often scarce. To address this, a technique called "prior laundering" uses an archive of legacy reconstructions to train the prior, which can lead to overconfidence when the inherited belief is tighter than the truth. This can result in deploying a diffusion prior that under-covers the operator's blind subspace, unlike a truth-trained control. The authors recommend reporting which directions the measurements resolve to separate confidence from inherited belief through the pipeline.

items.title: Simulation-Based Empirical Bayes
items.summary: Simulation-based empirical Bayes (SBEB) connects nonparametric EB to simulation-based inference by computing EB estimates using observed data, simulator samples, and an amortized inference network. SBEB iteratively refines the fitted EB prior toward the population prior without an explicit density. It demonstrates improved accuracy over standard SBI with a fixed prior in scientific applications.

items.title: Efficient Online LLM Watermark Detection via Rao-Blackwellized E-Processes
items.summary: Rao-Blackwellized e-processes enable efficient online watermark detection in large language models (LLMs), allowing for anytime-valid inference without storing full history. The framework reduces token-level dependence testing to a sequential testing problem with an explicit null distribution, achieving Type I error control under arbitrary optional stopping and positive asymptotic log-growth under watermarking.

items.title: Convergence analysis of a family of Zermelo-type iterations for the Bradley--Terry model
items.summary: A systematic local convergence analysis of the Bradley--Terry model's Zermelo-type iterations provides insight into the acceleration phenomenon for $\alpha=0$. The algorithm may fail to converge when $\alpha<1$, and its local convergence factor is quasi-convex in $\alpha$ under synchronous updates. In contrast, asynchronous updates are always locally convergent, with their local convergence factor provably monotonically increasing in $\alpha$, justifying the optimality of $\alpha=0$.

items.title: Variational Low-rank Tensor Decomposition for Multisubject Spatiotemporal Data Analysis
items.summary: ST-VTD framework combines tensor factorization with structured priors to jointly represent spatial maps and temporal dynamics, promoting a low-rank structure in spatial factors and adaptive dynamics in temporal factors. Posterior inference uses an amortized variational formulation with a warm-start strategy based on group independent component analysis, leading to an interpretable and parameter-efficient architecture. This approach significantly improves latent factor recovery compared to classical and probabilistic decomposition benchmarks.

items.title: General Value Functions for Remaining Useful Life and Failure-Mode Prediction
items.summary: Researchers developed General Value Functions (GVFs) for Remaining Useful Life and failure-mode prediction, improving predictions on event-triggered multimode simulation data by using a multi-step temporal-difference estimator, TD(n,λ). GVF predicts temporally consistent targets rather than independent window-level labels. The approach improves RUL and failure-mode prediction relative to supervised Monte Carlo control, especially under scarce complete labels.

items.title: Hopformer: Homogeneity-Pursuit Transformer for Time Series Forecasting
items.summary: Hopformer, a two-stage framework, addresses the challenge of forecasting multiple time-series with high-dimensional covariates. In the first stage, Sparsity Pattern Aggregation (SPA) extracts a common low-variance trend that incorporates covariates, acting as a homogenization layer. The second stage employs a LoRA-fine-tuned Transformer to model remaining complex dependencies in the residual. This method improves MASE by an average of 6.56% across synthetic and real-world forecasting benchmarks.

items.title: Learning Bidirectional Causal Interactions with Heteroscedastic Neural Networks
items.summary: SEMs-DNN, a heteroscedastic neural simultaneous-equation estimator, learns reciprocal structural interactions without external instruments. It jointly approximates nonlinear structural mean functions and feature-dependent variances using a diagonal Gaussian quasi-likelihood that incorporates the simultaneous-system Jacobian. SEM-DNN recovers structural effects more reliably than parametric, kernel-based, and separate-equation neural alternatives as information increases, although at greater computational cost.

items.title: Learning Ergodic Dynamical Systems from a Finite Trajectory
items.summary: Researchers Oleksii Kachaiev, Silvia Villa, and Lorenzo Rosasco present a method for learning from a single finite trajectory of an ergodic stochastic dynamical system. They focus on estimating the optimal one-step prediction function using nonlinear least squares and derive high-probability guarantees based on the invariant measure of the process. The approach combines tools from statistical learning theory and quantitative ergodic theory, relying on a concentration inequality for Hilbert-space-valued additive functionals of uniformly geometrically ergodic Markov chains.

items.title: Graph-Based Correlation Matrix Generation: A Convex Optimization Approach
items.summary: Researchers propose a convex optimization framework to generate theoretical correlation matrices with prescribed sparsity patterns associated with graph structures. The approach projects an initial matrix onto an elliptope under positive semidefiniteness constraints, enabling control over the mean of the off-diagonal entry distribution. Simulation studies illustrate the properties of generated matrices with respect to graph structure and demonstrate the flexibility of the method in generating realistic correlation matrices suitable for benchmarking statistical methods.
